summary: Takamaro Shigaraki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies. He served at Ryukoku University as faculty (1958), professor (1970), and president (1989–1995).

Takamatsu Yoshie studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, Waseda University, and the University of Paris. He taught at Waseda Junior and Senior High School (1906) and held positions at Waseda University as lecturer (1908, 1910), professor (1915), and dean (1930).

Takami Inoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Inoue was a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takamichi Fukita is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Taisho and Bukkyo universities under Shozen Kumoi, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Heinz Bechert. Fukita held posts at Bukkyo University (attested 1999 as lecturer, and 2013).

Takanobu Takahashi is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Rama. Periakaruppan, and Utrecht University. He held posts at International Buddhist University (1991) and the University of Tokyo (1996, 1999–2016).
Takanori Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. Kimura served as a lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996) and as head priest at Kaichōji (attested 2003).

Takanori Shintani works in religious studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University (~1968–1977) and held positions at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1999–2010) and Kokugakuin University (~2010–2019).

Takanori Unno specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Nagoya University under Yoshifumi Ueda, Hakuju Ui, and others, Unno held posts as assistant at Nagoya University, lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts, and professor at Meijo University (2002).

Takao Hayashi specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University, Kyoto University, and Brown University under David Pingree. His posts include researcher at Harish-Chandra Research Institute (1982–1983) and professor at Doshisha University (1995–2015).
Takao Kagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba, and served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

Takao Maruyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1957–1962). He held teaching posts at Rissho University (attested 1972, 1981), Shinshu University (attested 1983–1984; professor emeritus ~1995), and Mejiro University (attested 1988).

Takao Moriyasu worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies, history/archaeology, and sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Osaka University. His main appointments included associate professor at Kanazawa University (1982) and professor at Osaka University (1994–2012).
Takao Suita is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who held posts at Bukkyo University, including as a lecturer (attested 1997–2010, 2020).

Takao Yamagata was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1952–1961). He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1975–2003) and served as president of the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).

Takashi Hidaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a researcher at the Buddhism and Art Research Center at Otani University (2012) and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2014).

Takashi Iwata specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, Albrecht Wezler, Akira Hirakawa, and Ernst Steinkellner, and served as professor at Waseda University (~1991–2015).
Takashi Koezuka is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who held posts at Osaka University as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2012).
Takashi Maeda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied in the doctoral program at Tohoku University and served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995, 2006).

Takashi Nakao worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Rissho University and Tokyo University of Education. He was associate professor at Bunkyo University Women's College (~1965–1972) and professor (1979–2002) at Rissho University.

Takashi Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University, Peking University (1986–1989), and the University of Tokyo. He was appointed associate professor at Komazawa University in 1991.
